entries.title: Calendars & Trading Hours: Calendar
entries.notes: Current published holiday list (New Year's Day, Family Day, Good Friday, Victoria Day, Canada Day, Civic Holiday, Labour Day, Thanksgiving Day, Christmas Eve early close, Christmas Day, Boxing Day / "In Lieu of Boxing Day"). No entry for National Day for Truth and Reconciliation in either year, i.e. TSX does not close for it.

entries.title: TMX Group Holiday Operating Schedule (2025-12-03)
entries.notes: Confirms Wed Dec 24, 2025 open until 1:00 p.m. (TSX/TSXV), closed Thu Dec 25, Fri Dec 26, and Thu Jan 1, 2026 (no weekend shifting needed that year).

entries.title: TMX Group Holiday Operating Schedule (2023-12-05)
entries.notes: Closed Mon Dec 25, Tue Dec 26, 2023 and Mon Jan 1, 2024; no Dec 24 early-close line for TSX (Dec 24, 2023 was a Sunday, already non-trading).

entries.title: TMX Group Holiday Operating Schedule (December 2020 / January 2021)
entries.notes: Timetable for TSX/TSXV/TSX Alpha: Thu Dec 24, 2020 "Open until 1:00 p.m. (EST)"; closed Fri Dec 25, 2020, Mon Dec 28, 2020 "in lieu of Boxing Day" (Dec 26, 2020 was a Saturday) and Fri Jan 1, 2021. Confirms both the 2020 Dec 24 early close and the Boxing-Day-on-Saturday forward shift.

entries.title: TMX Group Holiday Operating Schedule (2021-11-30)
entries.notes: Primary source for the weekend-cascade case: Fri Dec 24, 2021 open until 1:00 p.m.; closed Mon Dec 27 ("in lieu of Christmas Day", nominal Sat Dec 25), Tue Dec 28 ("in lieu of Boxing Day", nominal Sun Dec 26), and Mon Jan 3, 2022 ("in lieu of New Year's Day", nominal Sat Jan 1, 2022). Confirms New Year's Day also uses next-available-weekday shifting (not forward-only).

entries.title: Toronto Stock Exchange, TSX Venture Exchange, TSX Alpha Exchange and Montréal Exchange Closed for Canada Day (2017-06-21)
entries.notes: Canada Day fell on Saturday, July 1, 2017; markets closed Monday, July 3, 2017 and reopened Tuesday, July 4.

entries.title: TMX Group notice: Canada Day 2023 (2023-06-28)
entries.notes: Canada Day fell on Saturday, July 1, 2023; markets closed Monday, July 3, 2023, reopened Tuesday, July 4. Confirms Canada Day cascades to the following Monday like the other statutory holidays, not to the preceding Friday.

entries.title: TMX Group Holiday Operating Schedule (2016-11-30)
entries.notes: Confirms, in TMX's own words, closed "Monday, December 26, 2016 in lieu of Christmas Day on Sunday, December 25, 2016" and "Tuesday, December 27, 2016 in lieu of Boxing Day on Monday, December 26, 2016": when Christmas Day (the chronologically earlier holiday) falls on a Sunday, it -- not Boxing Day -- takes the first available weekday, and Boxing Day cascades to the day after.

entries.title: TMX Group Holiday Operating Schedule (2022-12-07)
entries.notes: Corroborates the same pattern for 2022: closed Mon Dec 26, 2022, Tue Dec 27, 2022 and Mon Jan 2, 2023 "in lieu of" Christmas Day, Boxing Day and New Year's Day respectively (Dec 25, 2022 was a Sunday). Retrieved via search result summary; the source PDF itself returned HTTP 403 on direct fetch.

entries.title: TMX Markets Operating Schedule for National Day for Truth and Reconciliation (2021-08-11)
entries.notes: States plainly: "Toronto Stock Exchange, TSX Venture Exchange, and TSX Alpha Exchange will be open for trading on National Day of Truth and Reconciliation and regular operating hours will be in effect." Only Bourse de Montréal fixed-income derivatives close. TSX has never closed for this holiday since its creation in 2021; the current calendar page (`tsx-calendar-page`) confirms this is still true for 2025/2026.

entries.title: Holidays Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. H-5
entries.notes: Federal statute defining New Year's Day, Good Friday, Victoria Day ("the first Monday immediately preceding the 25th day of May"), Canada Day, Labour Day, Thanksgiving Day, Remembrance Day, and Christmas Day as legal holidays. Used for the Victoria Day date rule and to establish which TSX holidays are fixed by statute (as opposed to Civic Holiday, which is not).

entries.title: "Manitoba, Saskatchewan and Ontario Family Day" information notice (2007-10-16)
entries.publisher: Government of Canada, Treasury Board of Canada Secretariat
entries.notes: Records that Ontario's Family Day, third Monday of February, was first observed February 18, 2008 (Employment Standards Amendment Act (Family Day), 2007). TSX is an Ontario-based exchange whose published schedule (`tsx-calendar-page`) closes for every other Ontario statutory holiday, so it is modelled as closing for Family Day from its first year, 2008; no TMX press release from 2008 itself was found to confirm the very first occurrence directly.

entries.title: Toronto Stock Exchange Market Is Closed (11 September 2001)
entries.publisher: Toronto Stock Exchange (republished by Mondo Visione)
entries.notes: The exchange's release of 11 September 2001: "In response to the events today in the United States, the Toronto Stock Exchange has closed ... At the close of trading, the TSE 300 Composite Index was down 293.86 to 7050.84." A session with an official close, so the day is an unscheduled early termination, not a full closure. The release gives no halt time; CBC's 2002 anniversary report (cbc-2002-09-11-tsx) says the exchange "opened trading for 71 minutes before shutting down", i.e. about 10:41 ET, which is the only source for the time.

entries.title: Toronto Stock Exchange And CDNX Closed Wednesday, September 12, 2001
entries.publisher: Toronto Stock Exchange (republished by Mondo Visione)
entries.notes: "The TSE will remain closed today." The companion release of the same day, "Toronto Stock Exchange /CDNX To Reopen Thursday, September 13, 2001" (https://mondovisione.com/media-and-resources/news/toronto-stock-exchange-cdnx-to-reopen-thursday-september-13-2001-2011124/, preserved as tse-2001-09-13-reopen.html), confirms "the closing yesterday and again today" and the reopening "in the usual manner on Thursday, September 13, 2001". The noon pause on 14 September was a voluntary moment of silence, not a halt.

entries.title: TSX gains; U.S. markets falter on day of remembrance
entries.notes: Press: "The TSX opened trading for 71 minutes before shutting down until Sept. 13." The only source for the 2001-09-11 halt time (about 10:41 ET); the exchange's own release establishes the closure and the official close but not the time.

entries.title: Trading Resumes On Toronto Stock Exchange And TSX Venture Exchange (18 December 2008)
entries.notes: TMX's minute-by-minute incident overview for 17 December 2008: "9:30AM - Toronto Stock Exchange and TSX Venture Exchange opened for trading. 9:37AM - A problem with Level 1 ... 9:48AM - Trading was halted ... During the 18 minute session, approximately 28,000 trades occurred ... 2:30PM - The decision was made to remain closed for the day". TMX's own 2008 statistics count 251 trading days, one fewer than scheduled, so the exchange itself treats the day as a non-trading day; it is modelled as CLOSED with the 18-minute session recorded here. The same-day release "Toronto Stock Exchange And TSX Venture Exchange To Remain Closed For December 17, 2008" (https://mondovisione.com/media-and-resources/news/toronto-stock-exchange-and-tsx-venture-exchange-to-remain-closed-for-december-17-2011124/) states the exchange "will not resume trading today due to continuing technical issues with its data feeds".

entries.title: TMX Group Provides Update on Market Outage Incident and Confirms Readiness for Regular Market Opening Monday (28 April 2018)
entries.notes: "The outage, which began at 1:37:25 pm EDT Friday on MX and 1:39:13 pm EDT on TSX, TSXV, and TSX Alpha, was caused by a hardware failure in a central storage appliance of the trading system. ... Given the time of the incident, we could not engage disaster recovery systems in time to ensure an orderly market re-open and closing session." TMX Market Operations update #6 of 27 April 2018 (https://www.tsx.com/en/resource/1803, preserved as tmx-2018-04-27-market-ops-updates.pdf): "Trading will not resume today, including MOC." An unscheduled early termination at 13:39; the day remains a trading day (TMX's 2018 count deducts nothing for it).

entries.title: Incident Report: System Outage on TSX, TSXV, Alpha - Incident Date February 27, 2020
entries.notes: "The outage, which began at approximately 1:30pm ET was attributed to a system capacity issue within a messaging technology component of TMX's trading engine. ... After the trading application failure and full market halt at 1:54 pm, TMX's attempts to restart the trading complex encountered further complications that could not be resolved in a timely manner." No re-open and no closing auction; normal open on 28 February. An unscheduled early termination at 13:54; the day remains a trading day.

entries.title: Ops Notice 2022-012 - TMX Production Alert - Incident Report: System Outage on TSX, TSXV, TSX Alpha (1 November 2022)
entries.notes: Intraday halt from 10:04 to 11:10 EDT with a normal close: not a closure and not an early termination, so no row; cited so the absence is evidenced.

entries.title: Toronto Stock Exchange Statistics - December 2009
entries.notes: The exchange's year-end statistics release: year-to-date volume divided by the average daily volume (cross-checked with the transactions ratio) gives TMX's own count of trading days for the year and the previous year, counting the Christmas Eve 1 p.m. session as half a day. Every year 2008-2025 equals the scheduled count (weekdays minus the modelled closures) or that count less 0.5 for a weekday Christmas Eve, except 2008, which is one day short for 17 December 2008; so no other unscheduled full-day closure occurred, and the half-day accounting evidences a Christmas Eve early close in every weekday-24-December year from 2009.
